newsitem.title: USA: KinderCare says to merge in $600 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: KinderCare says to merge in $600 mln deal.

text.p: KinderCare Learning Centers Inc said Thursday it has signed a definitive agreement to merge with an affiliate of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co in a transaction valued at about $600 million.
Under the deal, KinderCare shareholders would receive $20.25 in cash for each share or would retain existing KinderCare common stock.
The election to retain stock is subject to proration so that about 93 percent of the outstanding KinderCare shares are exchanged for cash and about 7 percent are retained by existing shareholders.
Oaktree Capital Management LLC, a KinderCare affiliate, has agreed to retain a sufficient number of shares so that every other shareholder can receive cash if they so desire.
After the merger, an unidentified entity controlled by Kohlberg Kravis Roberts will own about 85 percent of KinderCare, and KinderCare's pre-merger shareholders will own the balance.
Also, after the merger, KinderCare will be capitalized with $175 million of equity, $148.75 million of which will be invested by an affiliate of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts.

The financing for the merger is being arranged by KinderCare, Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Chase Manhattan Corp. KinderCare also has secured commitments through Chase for a $300 million bank debt expansion facility to fund future growth and acquisitions.
The merger is expected to be completed by January 1997.
KinderCare is the largest preschool and child care company in the United States.
